docs.title: Assumptions, Risk, and Dependencies
docs.text:
This section outlines key assumptions, potential risks, and external dependencies that may influence the successful implementation and operation of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. Identifying these factors helps ensure that stakeholders maintain awareness of conditions that could impact project delivery, system adoption, and operational effectiveness.

The following subsections describe considerations related to project assumptions, potential risks, and external dependencies.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
This subsection describes conditions assumed to be true for the successful development and operation of the platform.

Examples of assumptions include:

  • Tenant organizations provide the necessary credit policies and approval structures required to configure the platform workflows.
  • Users responsible for reviewing and approving credit applications have appropriate training to operate the platform.
  • Supporting infrastructure required for the deployment and operation of the platform is available and maintained by the responsible parties

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
This subsection identifies external systems, organizational inputs, or operational factors that the platform depends on to function effectively.

Examples of dependencies include: - Availability of user access management and identity authentication services. - Integration with systems that may provide supporting customer or credit-related information. - Timely configuration and maintenance of approval matrices and operational policies by tenant administrators.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
This subsection outlines potential factors that could negatively affect the implementation, adoption, or operation of the platform.

Examples of risks include:

  • Delays in defining or configuring approval workflows may impact the readiness of the system for operational use.
  • Incomplete or inconsistent applicant information may lead to delays in the credit evaluation process.
  • Changes in regulatory or organizational policies may require adjustments to platform configuration or workflows.

docs.title: Business Context and Justification
docs.text:
This section describes the operational environment and business motivations behind the development of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. It outlines the current challenges associated with manual credit application processing, and explains how the proposed platform supports the automation and management of credit application workflows.

Understanding the business context provides stakeholders with insight into the problem being addressed and the expected benefits of implementing the platform.

docs.title: Business Objectives
docs.text:
The primary business objectives for implementing the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform include:

  • Standardization of credit application workflows
  • Reduction of manual intervention in routing and tracking
  • Improved visibility into application lifecycle stages
  • Centralized management of approval matrices
  • Enforcement of business rules governing eligibility and submission
  • Structured documentation and audit logging
  • Support for configurable, tenant-specific approval hierarchies

By digitizing and automating the credit origination process, financial institutions can improve operational efficiency while maintaining governance and control.

docs.title: Expected Business Impact
docs.text:
Implementation of the platform is expected to deliver measurable improvements across operational and governance functions, including:

  • Reduced average credit application processing time
  • Improved compliance traceability through structured audit logs
  • Enhanced role-based access control and accountability
  • Increased consistency in approval decision workflows
  • Improved applicant experience through standardized submission processes

The platform supports scalable operational growth by enabling financial institutions to manage increasing application volumes without proportional increases in manual effort.

docs.title: Current Operational Challenges
docs.text:
Financial institutions managing credit card applications often rely on semi-manual processes, including email-based document exchanges, spreadsheet tracking, and manual approval routing. These practices introduce operational inefficiencies and control risks.

Common challenges include:

  • Manual validation of submitted documents
  • Delayed routing of applications across approval hierarchies
  • Limited visibility into application status
  • Inconsistent enforcement of approval thresholds
  • Lack of centralized audit tracking
  • Dependency on email-based communication
  • Difficulty enforcing single active application rules

These processes increase turnaround time, elevate operational risk, and reduce transparency across credit review functions.

docs.title: High-Level Business Process Overview
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform supports a structured workflow that manages the lifecycle of credit card applications from submission to final decision. The platform provides a centralized environment where applicants, reviewers, and approvers interact through defined workflow stages governed by configurable business rules and approval hierarchies.

Operational workflows in the platform follow a consistent lifecycle pattern that includes request initiation, information submission, validation, review, routing, and outcome determination. The following workflows illustrate how the platform manages different credit-related processes

docs.title: Credit Amendment Workflow
docs.text:
The Credit Amendment Workflow allows authorized tenant users to initiate requests to modify or update previously approved credit application information.

This process supports operational scenarios where updates to customer information, credit limits, or supporting documentation are required after the initial approval:

  1. Amendment Request Initiation – A change or update request is initiated by an authorized tenant user to modify an existing credit application or credit account information.
  2. Validation – The system validates the eligibility conditions for the amendment, including verification of required fields and applicable business rules.
  3. Information Submission – Updated information or supporting documentation is provided to support the requested amendment.
  4. Routing – The amendment request is routed through the configured approval workflow to the appropriate authorized approvers.
  5. Outcome – The amendment request is either approved or rejected based on the review outcome.

This workflow ensures all updates to approved credit records undergo appropriate review and authorization.

Credit Amendment Workflow

docs.title: Credit Application Workflow
docs.text:
The Credit Application Workflow represents the primary process in the platform, enabling applicants to submit credit card applications and supporting documentation for review and approval.

The process typically follows these stages:

  1. Application Initiation - A new credit application is initiated by an authorized tenant user within the platform.
  2. Information Submission - The applicant provides the required information and uploads supporting documentation necessary for the credit application.
  3. Validation - The platform validates the completeness of required fields and verifies that submission rules are satisfied prior to further processing.
  4. Review - Authorized reviewers assess the submitted information and supporting documentation in accordance with the tenant organization's credit and compliance policies.
  5. Routing - The application is routed through the configured approval workflow to designated approvers based on approval thresholds and hierarchy rules.
  6. Outcome - The application is approved, rejected, or returned for additional information based on the review and approval decision. The platform maintains a complete audit trail of all actions performed during the application lifecycle.

Credit Application Workflow

docs.title: Credit Reinstatement Workflow
docs.text:
The Credit Reinstatement Workflow enables tenant organizations to process requests to reinstate credit privileges that were previously suspended, rejected, or inactive.

This process allows authorized users to submit reinstatement requests that are evaluated through the defined approval hierarchy:

  1. Reinstatement Request Initiation – A reinstatement request is submitted by an authorized tenant user for a previously suspended or inactive credit account.
  2. Validation – The system validates eligibility conditions for reinstatement, including completeness of required information and supporting documentation.
  3. Information Submission – Supporting documents and any required updated information are provided to support the reinstatement request.
  4. Routing – The reinstatement request is routed through the configured approval workflow to authorized reviewers.
  5. Outcome – The reinstatement request is either approved or rejected based on the review outcome.

The platform records all reinstatement activities to maintain transparency and auditability of credit decision processes.

docs.title: Business Requirements
docs.text:
This section defines the business requirements for the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform.

The requirements describe the expected system capabilities and operational behaviors necessary to support the credit card application lifecycle within tenant organizations.

The requirements are organized into functional areas aligned with the key operational processes introduced in the High-Level Business Process Overview section. Each functional area represents a group of related capabilities that support specific stages of the credit origination workflow, including application submission, document management, review and approval routing, and administrative configuration.

These requirements establish the functional expectations of the platform and provide the foundation for subsequent system design, development, and testing activities.

docs.title: Administrative Configuration
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing the administrative configuration capabilities of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. Administrative users must be able to manage system configuration settings that support the operational workflows of the platform, including approval routing structures, role assignments, and system-level parameters.

Administrative configuration capabilities allow tenant organizations to adapt the platform to their internal governance structures, and operational policies while maintaining control over access permissions and approval hierarchies.

Administrative Configuration

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.8-01 Approval Matrix Configuration The system shall allow authorized administrative users to configure approval matrices that determine the routing of applications through the review and approval workflow. BR-6.8-02 Role Configuration The system shall allow administrative users to assign and manage user roles within the tenant organization. BR-6.8-03 Permission Management The system shall enforce permissions associated with user roles to control access to system functions and data. BR-6.8-04 Requirements List Configuration The system shall allow administrative users to configure the list of required documents or information needed for credit application submissions. BR-6.8-05 System Parameter Configuration The system shall allow administrative users to configure system parameters that influence operational behavior of the platform. BR-6.8-06 Administrative Audit Visibility The system shall allow administrative users to review system activity logs and configuration changes.

docs.title: Authentication and Access Control
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing how users access the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform and how permissions are managed within the system:

  • Authentication Mechanisms ensure that only authorized users can access the platform
  • Access Control rules determine the actions each user role is permitted to perform within the credit origination workflow.

The platform supports secure authentication for both external applicants and internal tenant users, while enforcing role-based access control to protect sensitive financial and personal information associated with credit applications.

Authentication and Access Control

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.1-01 Applicant Access The system shall allow applicants to access the platform using registered credentials to initiate and manage credit card applications. BR-6.1-02 Tenant User Authentication The system shall allow tenant users to securely authenticate in order to access operational functions associated with credit application review, approval, and administration. BR-6.1-03 Role-Based Access Control The system shall enforce role-based access control to ensure that users can only perform actions permitted by their assigned role. BR-6.1-04 Session Management The system shall maintain authenticated user sessions and automatically terminate inactive sessions after a defined period of inactivity. BR-6.1-05 Access Restriction for Unauthorized Users The system shall prevent unauthorized users from accessing application data, administrative functions, or workflow activities. BR-6.1-06 Administrative User Management The system shall allow authorized administrators to manage user accounts, assign roles, and configure user permissions within the tenant environment.

docs.title: Credit Amendment Processes
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing the amendment or update of previously submitted or approved credit applications. Operational scenarios may arise where information associated with an application must be corrected, updated, or revised after the initial submission or approval.

The platform supports a controlled amendment process that allows authorized tenant users to submit update requests while ensuring that such changes undergo appropriate review and authorization. This process ensures that modifications to credit records are tracked, validated, and approved in accordance with the organization's credit governance policies.

Credit Amendment Processes

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.5-01 Amendment Request Initiation The system shall allow authorized tenant users to initiate a credit amendment request for an existing application record. BR-6.5-02 Amendment Eligibility Validation The system shall validate whether the application is eligible for amendment based on defined businessrules. BR-6.5-03 Submission of Updated Information The system shall allow users to provide updated information or documentation as part of the amendment request. BR-6.5-04 Amendment Workflow Routing The system shall route amendment requests through the configured approval workflow based on the tenant organization’s approval hierarchy. BR-6.5-05 Amendment Approval Decision The system shall allow authorized approvers to approve or reject amendment requests. BR-6.5-06 Amendment Status Tracking The system shall maintain a status indicator reflecting the progress of the amendment request throughout the review process. BR-6.5-07 Amendment History Recording The system shall record amendment actions and decisions associated with an application to maintain a complete audit history.

docs.title: Credit Application Submission
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing the creation and submission of credit card applications in the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. The platform supports the following processes:

  • Collection of applicant information
  • Submission of supporting documentation
  • Enforcement of submission rules before an application is routed for review

These requirements ensure that applications are submitted with complete and valid information while maintaining consistency and traceability throughout the credit origination process.

Credit Application Submission

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.2-01 Application Creation The system shall allow authorized users to create a new credit card application in the platform. BR-6.2-02 Single Active Application Rule The system shall enforce a rule that prevents the creation of multiple active credit applications for the same applicant. BR-6.2-03 Required Information Capture The system shall require applicants to provide mandatory information necessary to evaluate the credit application prior to submission. BR-6.2-04 Supporting Document Upload The system shall allow applicants to upload supporting documents required for credit evaluation. BR-6.2-05 Accepted File Formats The system shall support predefined file formats for uploaded documents. BR-6.2-06 File Size Limitation The system shall enforce file size limits for uploaded documents to ensure system performance and storage efficiency. BR-6.2-07 Application Validation The system shall validate that all required information and documentation have been provided before an application can be submitted for review. BR-6.2-08 Application Submission The system shall allow applicants or authorized tenant users to submit completed applications for review. BR-6.2-09 Submission Locking The system shall prevent modification of an application once it has been submitted for review, unless it is returned for correction by an authorized reviewer. BR-6.2-10 Application Status Tracking The system shall assign and maintain a status indicator to track the progress of the application throughout the review and approval process.

docs.title: Credit Reinstatement Processes
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing the reinstatement of credit privileges within the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. In certain operational scenarios, previously suspended, rejected, or inactive credit applications may require reassessment to determine whether credit privileges can be restored.

The platform supports a reinstatement workflow that allows authorized tenant users to submit reinstatement requests and route them through the appropriate review and approval hierarchy. This process ensures that reinstatement decisions are evaluated according to the organization’s credit governance policies while maintaining traceability of all actions performed.

Credit Reinstatement Processes

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.6-01 Reinstatement Request Initiation The system shall allow authorized tenant users to initiate a credit reinstatement request for an existing application or credit record. BR-6.6-02 Reinstatement Eligibility Validation The system shall validate whether the application or credit record is eligible for reinstatement based on defined business rules. BR-6.6-03 Supporting Documentation Submission The system shall allow users to provide supporting information or documentation required to evaluate the reinstatement request. BR-6.6-04 Reinstatement Workflow Routing The system shall route reinstatement requests through the configured approval workflow in accordance with the tenant organization's approval hierarchy. BR-6.6-05 Reinstatement Decision Recording The system shall allow authorized approvers to approve or reject reinstatement requests. BR-6.6-06 Reinstatement Status Tracking The system shall maintain a status indicator reflecting the progress of the reinstatement request throughout the evaluation process. BR-6.6-07 Reinstatement Audit Logging The system shall record all reinstatement actions and decisions to maintain an audit trail of the reinstatement process.

docs.title: Document Management
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements related to the handling, storage, and management of supporting documents associated with credit applications. Supporting documentation is a critical component of the credit evaluation process, as reviewers and approvers rely on submitted documents to verify applicant information and assess credit eligibility.

The platform provides mechanisms that securely store submitted documents, associate them with the appropriate application records, and allow authorized users to review these documents during the evaluation process.

Document Management

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.3-01 Document Attachment to Application The system shall associate uploaded documents with the corresponding credit application record. BR-6.3-02 Document Accessibility for Reviewers The system shall allow authorized tenant users to access and review documents submitted as part of a credit application. BR-6.3-03 Document Type Identification The system shall allow uploaded documents to be categorized according to predefined document types required for credit evaluation. BR-6.3-04 Document Integrity Preservation The system shall store uploaded documents without altering their original content. BR-6.3-05 Document Validation by Reviewers The system shall allow authorized reviewers to validate the completeness and relevance of submitted documents as part of the credit review process. BR-6.3-06 Document Retention The system shall retain documents associated with credit applications for reference and audit purposes.

docs.title: Reporting and Audit Capabilities
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements for reporting and audit-related capabilities in the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform:

  • Reporting functions allow tenant users to monitor application activity, review application status, and generate operational reports to support credit management activities.
  • Audit capabilities ensure that all actions performed within the platform are recorded and traceable. Maintaining a complete audit trail supports operational transparency, internal governance, and regulatory compliance requirements associated with credit decision processes.

Reporting and Audit Capabilities

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.7-01 Application Listing The system shall provide a listing of credit applications accessible to authorized tenant users. BR-6.7-02 Application Filtering The system shall allow users to filter application records based on predefined criteria such as application status, submission date, or applicant information. BR-6.7-03 Application Detail Viewing The system shall allow authorized users to view detailed information associated with individual credit applications. BR-6.7-04 Report Export Capability The system shall allow users to export application data for reporting and analysis purposes. BR-6.7-05 Approval History Visibility The system shall display the history of review and approval actions associated with each application. BR-6.7-06 Audit Log Recording The system shall record user activities and workflow actions performed within the platform. BR-6.7-07 Audit Log Accessibility The system shall allow authorized administrative users to access audit logs for monitoring and investigation purposes.

docs.title: Risk Review and Approval Workflow
docs.text:
This subsection defines the requirements governing the review and approval of credit card applications within the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. After an application has been submitted, it undergoes a structured evaluation process to verify the completeness of submitted information, assess credit eligibility, and ensure compliance with the tenant organization's credit policies.

The platform supports configurable approval workflows that route applications to appropriate reviewers and approvers based on predefined approval matrices and role hierarchies. These workflows ensure that credit decisions are reviewed and authorized according to the organization's governance requirements while maintaining transparency and auditability throughout the decision process.

Risk Review and Approval Workflow

No. Business Requirement Definition BR-6.4-01 Application Review Access The system shall allow authorized reviewers to access submitted credit applications for evaluation. BR-6.4-02 Document and Data Review The system shall allow reviewers to examine submitted application data and supporting documentation before making a decision. BR-6.4-03 Configurable Approval Routing The system shall route applications through a configurable approval workflow based on predefined approval matrices. BR-6.4-04 Approval Decision Recording The system shall allow authorized approvers to record approval or rejection decisions for submitted applications. BR-6.4-05 Return for Correction The system shall allow reviewers or approvers to return an application to the applicant or initiating user for correction or completion. BR-6.4-06 Mandatory Decision Comments The system shall require users performing approval, rejection, or return actions to provide comments explaining the decision. BR-6.4-07 Application Status Updates The system shall update application status automatically as it progresses through the review and approval workflow. BR-6.4-08 Approval History Tracking The system shall record all review and approval actions associated with an application to maintain a complete audit trail. BR-6.4-09 Notification of Workflow Actions The system shall notify relevant users when an application requires review, approval, or additional information.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This document outlines the business requirements for the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform, a multi-tenant SaaS solution designed to automate the credit card application and approval process. The document describes the objectives of the platform, the operational context in which it will be used, and the functional capabilities required to support credit application management.

The purpose of this document is to provide a clear understanding of the business needs and system expectations that guides the design, development, and implementation of the platform.

docs.title: Product Purpose and Terminology
docs.text: This section introduces the purpose and scope of the Business Requirement Document, provides an overview of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform, and defines the key terms used throughout the documentation.

docs.title: Purpose of the Document
docs.text:
This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the business and operational requirements for the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform.

This document establishes the scope, functional expectations, and business rules governing the platform’s core processes, including credit application submission, review and approval workflows, amendment requests, and reinstatement processing.

This document aims to:

  • Provide a structured definition of business requirements.
  • Align stakeholders on functional scope and operational expectations.
  • Serve as the foundation for subsequent system, functional, and technical design documentation.
  • Support traceability across design, development, testing, and validation activities.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform enables financial institutions to standardize and digitize their credit card application lifecycle processes through a configurable, role-based workflow engine.

The platform supports:

  • Applicant-initiated credit application submission
  • Multi-level risk and compliance review
  • Configurable approval routing
  • Document management and audit logging
  • Credit amendment and reinstatement processes
  • Administrative configuration of approval matrices and requirement lists

The platform is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS solution, enabling tenant organizations to configure approval logic, role hierarchies, and operational parameters independently while maintaining data isolation.

docs.title: Definitions and Terminology
docs.text:
This section defines the key terms and concepts used throughout the document.

Term Definition Applicant An external customer applying for credit. Approval Matrix A configurable routing logic defining approval hierarchy and thresholds. Approval Workflow The sequence of review and approval steps required before a credit application receives a final decision. Approver/ Reviewer An authorized tenant personnel responsible for evaluating applications. Audit Trail A record of actions and decisions performed within the system for monitoring and compliance purposes. Credit Origination The end-to-end process of accepting, reviewing, approving, or rejecting a credit card application. Reinstatement A process to restore credit privileges following suspension or rejection. Tenant Organization A financial institution subscribed to the CardFlow platform. Tenant User A user who belongs to a tenant organization and is authorized to access and perform operational functions in the platform based on assigned roles and permissions.

docs.title: Regulatory and Compliance Considerations
docs.text:
Financial institutions operate within regulated environments where credit decisions, customer information, and financial records must be handled in accordance with applicable regulatory and governance requirements. The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform must therefore support operational controls that enable tenant organizations to maintain compliance with relevant financial regulations, internal policies, and data protection standards.

The platform provides mechanisms that promote transparency, traceability, and responsible handling of sensitive customer information throughout the credit application lifecycle.

The following subsections outline key regulatory and compliance considerations relevant to the platform’s operation.

docs.title: Data Protection and Privacy
docs.text:
This subsection outlines considerations related to the protection, access control, and secure handling of applicant data processed within the platform.

  • The platform supports the responsible handling of applicant information and sensitive financial data in accordance with applicable data protection requirements. Access to customer data is restricted to authorized users, and the platform enforces role-based access controls to prevent unauthorized access to personal or financial information.
  • The platform maintains secure storage of documents and information submitted as part of credit applications, ensuring that sensitive data is accessible only to users with appropriate permissions.

docs.title: Data Retention
docs.text:
This subsection discusses considerations related to the storage and retention of application records, documents, and system activity logs for governance and audit purposes.

  • The platform maintains records of submitted applications, supporting documents, and audit logs for reference and compliance purposes. Retained records allow tenant organizations to review historical application activity and maintain documentation required for audit and regulatory review.
  • Retention policies may be defined according to the tenant organization's internal governance policies and applicable regulatory requirements.

docs.title: Financial Regulatory Requirements
docs.text:
This subsection describes how the platform supports transparency and traceability of actions performed throughout the credit application lifecycle.

  • Credit approval decisions require transparency and traceability to support internal governance and regulatory oversight. The platform maintains a record of actions performed throughout the credit application lifecycle, including application submission, review actions, approval decisions, and administrative configuration changes.
  • These records allow tenant organizations to review historical activity and support audit investigations when necessary.

docs.title: KYC/AML Integration Considerations
docs.text:
This subsection highlights how the platform supports tenant organizations in performing customer verification activities that may be required as part of credit evaluation processes.

  • Financial institutions may require verification of customer identity and supporting documentation as part of the credit application evaluation process. The platform supports the submission and review of documentation that may be used to assist tenant organizations in performing Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) verification activities.
  • Tenant organizations may incorporate these verification activities into their internal credit review workflows as required by their operational policies.

docs.title: Scope Definition
docs.text: This section defines the functional boundaries of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. It outlines the key operational capabilities included in the platform, and the areas that are explicitly excluded from the current scope of implementation.

docs.title: Future Considerations
docs.text:
The platform architecture allowds extensibility to support:

  • Integration with external credit bureau APIs
  • Advanced risk scoring services
  • Automated document verification services
  • Expanded reporting analytics
  • Regional compliance configuration

Note: Future enhancements may be defined under separate requirement documentation.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform supports the following functional areas within the credit card origination lifecycle:

  • Credit Application Submission
    • Applicant registration and authentication
    • Creation of new credit card applications
    • Enforcement of one active application per applicant
    • Pre-population of available customer data
    • Upload of supporting documentation
    • Validation of required fields prior to submission
    • Submission locking upon finalization
  • Multi-Level Review and Approval Workflow
    • Configurable approval matrix based on defined thresholds
    • Routing of applications to reviewers and approvers
    • Support for manual reassignment where necessary
    • Return-to-applicant functionality for incomplete submissions
    • Mandatory comment capture for approval, rejection, or return actions
    • Automatic notification triggers at defined workflow stages
  • Credit Amendment / Update Process
    • Initiation of update requests for approved applications
    • Restriction of updates when other active applications exist
    • Approval routing consistent with configurable workflow rules
    • Locking of records post-submission
  • Credit Reinstatement Process
    • Initiation of reinstatement requests by authorized tenant users
    • Workflow routing based on configured approval hierarchy
    • Status tracking and notification upon decision
  • Document Management
    • Support for predefined file formats (for example, PDF, JPG, PNG)
    • Enforcement of file size limits
    • Storage of uploaded documents linked to application records
    • Manual validation of document contents by authorized reviewers
  • Reporting and Audit Capabilities
    • Application listing and filtering by status, date, and role
    • Export capability for reporting purposes
    • Capture of approval history and decision logs
    • Audit trail visibility for administrative users
  • Administrative Configuration
    • Configuration of approval matrices
    • Management of requirement lists
    • Role configuration and permission management
    • Access to audit logs
    • System-level configuration controls

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text: The following areas are explicitly excluded from the scope of this platform: - Core banking ledger management - Credit scoring algorithm design or external bureau computation logic - Card manufacturing and issuance processes - Payment processing and settlement systems - Fraud detection engine implementation - Direct integration with third-party ERP systems unless defined in a future phase

docs.title: Stakeholders and User Roles
docs.text:
This section discusses the primary stakeholders involved in the operation and use of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. These stakeholders represent the roles responsible for initiating:

  • Credit applications
  • Reviewing submitted information
  • Approving or rejecting applications
  • Managing system configuration and oversight

Understanding the responsibilities of each stakeholder group ensures the platform supports the operational workflows, approval hierarchies, and governance requirements associated with credit application processing.

docs.title: Platform Operations
docs.text:
Platform Operations represent the service provider responsible for maintaining the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. This group ensures the availability, reliability, and security of the platform and may perform system-level configuration, monitoring, and maintenance activities.

Platform Operations do not participate in the credit decision process but provide the infrastructure and operational support required for Tenant Organizations to use the platform effectively.

docs.title: Tenant Organizations
docs.text:
Tenant Organizations are financial institutions subscribed to the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. Each tenant operates in its own isolated environment and configures approval workflows, role assignments, and operational rules according to its internal credit governance policies.

Tenant Users are responsible for managing the credit application lifecycle in their organization, including submission, review, approval, and administrative configuration activities.

docs.title: User Role Definitions
docs.text:
The platform supports multiple user roles aligned with the operational stages of the credit origination workflow. Each role is granted permissions appropriate to its responsibilities in the credit review and approval process.

Typical roles supported by the platform include:

User Role Definitions Term | Definition ---|--- Applicant | External customer submitting a credit card application and required supporting documentation. Sales Officer | Tenant User responsible for assisting applicants and initiating credit application submissions. Risk Reviewer | Tenant user responsible for reviewing application details and assessing credit risk before approval decisions. Compliance | Reviewer Tenant user responsible for verifying regulatory and documentation requirements prior to approval. Approver | Authorized personnel responsible for approving or rejecting applications based on defined approval thresholds. Platform Administrator | Tenant User responsible for managing configuration settings, approval matrices, user roles, and system parameters in the tenant environment.

docs.title: Success Criteria and KPIs
docs.text:
This section defines the key indicators used to measure the effectiveness and operational impact of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform after implementation. These indicators help evaluate whether the platform achieves its objective of improving efficiency, reducing manual intervention, and enhancing visibility across the credit application process.

The success of the platform is assessed through measurable improvements in application processing efficiency, workflow transparency, and operational control.

docs.title: Application Processing Efficiency
docs.text:
The platform improves the efficiency of the credit application process by reducing the time required to submit, review, and approve credit applications.

Example indicators may include:

  • Reduction in average application processing time
  • Increased number of applications processed within a given period
  • Reduced manual effort required to manage application submissions

docs.title: Operational Efficiency
docs.text:
The platform enhances operational efficiency by automating manual tasks associated with credit application handling and approval coordination.

Example indicators may include:

  • Reduction in manual document handling
  • Reduced dependency on email-based approvals
  • Improved coordination between reviewers and approvers

docs.title: Reporting and Monitoring Capability
docs.text:
The platform enables tenant organizations to generate operational reports and monitor system activity to support management oversight and decision-making.

Example indicators may include:

  • Availability of exportable application reports
  • Access to audit logs for monitoring system activities
  • Improved ability to review application trends and operational performance

docs.title: Workflow Visibility and Traceability
docs.text:
The platform provides improved visibility into the status and progression of credit applications across the approval workflow.

Example indicators may include:

  • Ability to track application status in real time
  • Availability of approval history for submitted applications
  • Improved monitoring of pending or delayed applications

docs.title: Architecture Considerations
docs.text:
This section describes the key architectural considerations applied during the design of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform to support scalability, maintainability, security, auditability, and tenant isolation within the multi-tenant SaaS environment.

The platform architecture is designed to support the following while maintaining separation between tenant environments and supporting enterprise-level operational requirements:

  • Workflow-driven processing
  • Configurable business rules
  • Secure operational handling
  • Sustainable system growth

docs.title: Auditability
docs.text:
The platform architecture supports auditability by recording workflow activities, approval actions, validation events, state transitions, and system-generated operations throughout the request lifecycle.

Auditability considerations include:

  • Workflow traceability across lifecycle stages
  • Recording of user and system actions
  • Audit preservation for operational review
  • Tracking of workflow state transitions
  • Notification and approval event logging
  • Support for reporting and compliance review activities

docs.title: Maintainability
docs.text:
The platform architecture is designed to support maintainability by organizing system capabilities into modular functional components and clearly separated architectural layers. This structure allows workflow logic, validation rules, integrations, reporting services, and notification behavior to be updated or extended with minimal impact on other platform components.

Maintainability considerations include:

  • Modular service-oriented architecture
  • Separation of business rules and workflow logic
  • Configurable workflow and approval processing
  • Centralized validation and notification handling
  • Structured audit and reporting capabilities

docs.title: Scalability
docs.text:
The platform architecture supports scalability by separating presentation, application processing, workflow orchestration, data management, and integration services into distinct architectural layers. This separation allows the platform to support increasing users, tenants, workflow transactions, and operational workloads without significantly impacting overall system behavior.

Scalability considerations include:

  • Support for multiple tenant organizations
  • Separation of processing services and data management
  • Expandable workflow and approval processing
  • Support for increasing workflow volumes and concurrent users
  • Flexible integration capabilities for external systems and services

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The platform architecture incorporates security controls to support secure access management, tenant-level isolation, controlled workflow access, and protection of sensitive application and customer information.

Security considerations include:

  • Authentication and authorization enforcement
  • Role-based access control (RBAC)
  • Tenant-specific access boundaries
  • Controlled access to workflow and reporting functions
  • Secure handling of documents and audit records
  • Protection of workflow and application data

docs.title: Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
The platform architecture supports tenant isolation by logically separating tenant-specific users, workflow configurations, approval rules, documents, and operational data within the shared SaaS environment.

Tenant isolation considerations include:

  • Tenant-specific access control
  • Logical separation of workflow and application data
  • Tenant-level configuration management
  • Segregated reporting and operational visibility
  • Controlled access to tenant-owned records and documents
  • Secure handling of tenant-specific workflow operations

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: This section provides a high-level overview of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform architecture, highlighting its solution structure, core capabilities, and design principles. The platform is designed to support configurable credit origination workflows while maintaining scalability, security, auditability, maintainability, and tenant isolation in a multi-tenant SaaS environment.

docs.title: Architectural Principles
docs.text:
The architectural design of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform is guided by principles intended to support operational consistency, maintainability, scalability, and secure workflow processing.

Architectural Principles Principle | Description --- | --- Scalability | The architecture supports growth in transaction volume, tenants, and workflow processing activities. Maintainability | Architectural components are logically separated to simplify updates and maintenance. Configurability | Workflow behavior, routing logic, and operational rules can be configured per tenant. Auditability | Workflow actions and decisions are recorded to support traceability and governance. Security | Role-based access control and secure data handling mechanisms are enforced. Reusability | Shared workflow services and validation components are reused across workflows. Extensibility | Additional workflows and integrations can be introduced with minimal architectural impact.

docs.title: Architectural Style
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform adopts a layered service-oriented architecture designed to separate presentation, workflow processing, business logic, data management, and integration responsibilities into logically organized architectural components. The architecture follows the following design principles:

  • Separation of concerns across architectural layers
  • Centralized workflow orchestration and lifecycle management
  • Configurable business rule processing
  • Role-based interaction and authorization
  • Modular service interaction
  • Tenant-aware data and configuration isolation
  • Traceable and auditable workflow execution

The platform architecture is designed to support future extensibility by allowing additional workflow types, integrations, reporting capabilities, and operational configurations to be introduced without significantly impacting existing system components.

docs.title: Core Architectural Capabilities
docs.text:
The architecture supports several core platform capabilities required for credit origination processing and workflow automation.

  • Workflow Management – The platform provides centralized workflow orchestration for credit application, amendment, and reinstatement processing, supporting lifecycle transitions from initiation through outcome processing.
  • Validation and Eligibility Processing – Validation services enforce mandatory field requirements, document requirements, eligibility conditions, and input constraints before requests are allowed to proceed within the workflow.
  • Review and Approval Processing – The platform supports configurable review and approval workflows, including reviewer actions, approval routing, decision recording, returned requests, and rejection handling.
  • Document Management – The architecture supports secure upload, association, retrieval, and management of supporting documents linked to workflow requests and applications.
  • Audit and Traceability – Audit services record workflow actions, approval decisions, status transitions, validation outcomes, and user interactions to support operational traceability and compliance monitoring.
  • Multi-Tenant Configuration – Tenant-specific configuration capabilities allow organizations to maintain independent workflow rules, approval routing behavior, operational settings, and user access structures within the shared SaaS environment.

docs.title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture Context
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform operates in a multi-tenant SaaS architecture model where multiple tenant organizations share a common application environment while maintaining logical separation of data, workflow configurations, user access controls, and operational policies.

The architecture ensures that:

  • Tenant-specific data remains logically isolated.
  • Workflow configurations can vary per tenant organization.
  • User access permissions are managed independently per tenant.
  • Reporting and audit visibility are restricted according to tenant boundaries.
  • Shared platform services can support multiple tenant environments simultaneously.

This architecture model enables centralized platform management while supporting configurable operational behavior across participating organizations.

Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture Context

docs.title: Solution Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform is a multi-tenant SaaS solution designed to automate and manage the end-to-end lifecycle of credit origination processes, including credit application submission, amendment processing, reinstatement processing, validation, review, routing, approval, and outcome management.

The platform provides a centralized environment where applicants, tenant users, reviewers, approvers, and administrative users interact with configurable workflow-driven services to process requests according to defined business rules and operational policies.

The solution architecture is structured around the following primary architectural domains.

Primary Architectural Layer

Architectural Layer Description External Users Users and stakeholders that interact with the platform to initiate, process, review, approve, and manage requests. Presentation Layers Provides web-based interfaces for applicants, tenant users, reviewers, approvers, and administrators. Security and Access Control Layer Enforces authentication, authorization, RBAC, tenant isolation, and secure access management. Application Services Layer Handles workflow orchestration, validation, routing, notifications, audit operations, and reporting services. Business Rules and Workflow Layer Applies workflow logic, validation rules, eligibility checks, routing conditions, and state transition rules. Data Management Layer Manages application data, workflow records, documents, user information, and audit logs. Integration Layer Supports communication with external systems and third-party services.

Solution Architecture Overview

The platform architecture supports configurable workflow processing to allow tenant organizations to adapt approval structures, routing behavior, validation logic, and operational rules based on business requirements.

These assumptions and constraints help define the expected operating conditions, integration dependencies, workflow behavior, and architectural boundaries of the platform in the multi-tenant SaaS environment.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
The following assumptions were considered during the architectural design of the platform:

Assumptions

Assumption Description Cloud-Based Deployment The platform is deployed in a cloud-hosted SaaS environment. Tenant-Based Operations Multiple tenant organizations share the platform while maintaining logical data and access isolation. Role-Based Access Control Users are assigned roles that define workflow access and operational permissions. Workflow-Driven Processing Credit application, amendment, and reinstatement requests follow defined workflow lifecycle stages. External Service Availability External authentication, notification, and integration services are assumed to be operational and accessible when required. Browser-Based Access Users access the platform through supported web browsers and secured network connections. Configurable Workflow Rules Workflow routing, approval conditions, and validation rules are configurable at the tenant or platform level. Audit Preservation Workflow actions and system-generated events are recorded and retained for operational traceability.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
The following constraints apply to the architectural design and operational behavior of the platform:

Constraints

Constraint Description Shared SaaS Infrastructure Multiple tenant organizations operate in a shared platform environment. Tenant Isolation Requirements Tenant data and workflow operations must remain logically segregated. Dependency on External Services Authentication providers, notification services, and external systems may impact workflow processing if unavailable. Workflow Dependency Request processing is dependent on configured workflow definitions, routing rules, and approval structures. Role-Based Operational Limits User actions are restricted based on assigned roles and permissions. docs.text: This section describes how the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform integrates with external systems and third-party services to support authentication, workflow processing, notification delivery, and data exchange. docs.title: API Architecture
docs.text:
This subsection describes how API-based interactions are structured within the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform. APIs allow internal and external systems to exchange data securely with the platform while supporting workflow-related operations such as application creation, data retrieval, status updates, and external validation.

The API architecture supports: - Secure API access through authentication and authorization. - Request validation before processing. - Controlled access to application and workflow data. - Integration with workflow, validation, document, audit, and notification services. - Consistent response handling for successful and failed API requests.

When an external system sends a request to create a credit application:

  1. The request enters through the API Gateway / Integration Layer.
  2. The Security & Access Control layer checks authentication and permissions.
  3. The request is passed to the Application Service.
  4. The Validation Engine checks required data.
  5. The Workflow Engine creates the workflow record.
  6. The Data Management Layer stores the application.
  7. The Audit & Logging component records the event.

API Architecture

Integration Layer/ API Gateway | Entry point for API requests. It receives requests, routes them, and standardizes communication. Security & Access Control | Verifies whether the request is authenticated and authorized before allowing access. Application Services | Handles the actual business operation, such as creating an application, validating data, updating workflow status, sending notifications, or writing audit logs. Data Management Layer | Stores or retrieves application records, documents, workflow data, and audit logs.

After delivery, the platform records the notification event for audit and reference purposes.

docs.title: Audit and Traceability
docs.text:
This subsection describes the audit and traceability mechanisms implemented within the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform to support workflow transparency, operational monitoring, compliance tracking, and historical record preservation.

The platform records workflow-related activities and system events throughout the request lifecycle, including:

  • Request creation and submission
  • Validation events
  • Workflow state transitions
  • Review and approval decisions
  • User actions and updates
  • Notification activities
  • Administrative configuration changes

  • Historical activity tracking

docs.title: Authentication and Access Control
docs.text:
This subsection describes the authentication and authorization mechanisms used by the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform to control access to system resources and workflow operations.

The platform enforces role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure that users can only access functions, workflow actions, records, and administrative capabilities permitted by their assigned roles and tenant-specific permissions.

The security and access control architecture supports:

  • User authentication and session management
  • Role-based access control (RBAC)
  • Tenant-level data isolation
  • Permission-based workflow access
  • Controlled administrative access
  • Secure credential validation
  • Authorization enforcement across workflow stages

The platform supports multiple user roles, including applicants, tenant users, reviewers, approvers, and administrators, each with distinct operational permissions and workflow responsibilities.

docs.title: Data Protection
docs.text:
This subsection describes the data protection mechanisms implemented within the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform to support secure storage, transmission, and handling of application and customer information.

The platform applies security controls and protection mechanisms designed to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and controlled access of sensitive workflow and customer data within the multi-tenant SaaS environment.

Data protection measures include:

  • Secure transmission of data between platform components
  • Controlled access to sensitive records and documents
  • Tenant-level data segregation
  • Protection of uploaded documents and audit records
  • Controlled access to workflow and reporting information
  • Secure handling of authentication and session information
  • Audit preservation and traceability controls

The platform architecture is designed to support secure operational processing while maintaining workflow accessibility, auditability, and tenant-specific access boundaries across the system.

docs.title: Workflow Architecture

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
This section addresses common questions related to the use of CardFlow Credit Origination Platform.

  • How can I check the status of my application?

    Navigate to Applications or Requests and review the Current Status column. You may also open the application to view detailed workflow progress.

  • What does the Returned status mean?

    Returned indicates that additional information, supporting documentation, or corrections are required before processing can continue.

  • Can I modify an application after submission?

    Submitted applications generally cannot be edited unless they are returned for correction or an authorized amendment process is initiated.

  • How can I view workflow history?

    Open the application and review the Workflow History section to view status changes, user actions, and processing milestones.

  • Can I download application information?

    Yes. Authorized users may export application, workflow, approval, and audit information using the Reports module.

  • Why am I unable to approve a request?

    Possible reasons include:

    • Required validations are incomplete
    • Supporting documents are missing
    • Approval prerequisites have not been satisfied
    • You do not have approval permissions
    • Review the approval requirements checklist for additional details.

  • Who can view audit history?

    Audit history is typically available only to authorized users such as reviewers, approvers, administrators, auditors, or compliance personnel, depending on assigned permissions.

  • How do I change my notification preferences?

    Navigate to Notifications and update the notification channels and event types that you wish to receive.

docs.title: Credit Amendment Requests
docs.text: The Credit Amendment feature allows authorized users to request changes to existing credit applications or account information. Amendment requests undergo validation, review, and approval before any changes are applied to the selected record.

docs.title: Creating an Amendment Request
docs.text:
Create an amendment request to initiate modifications to an existing application or account. To create an amendment request:

  1. Open the application or account record. Creating an Amendment Request – Create an Amendment Request Button
  2. Click Create Amendment Request. Create Amendment Request screen displays. Creating an Amendment Request – Create Amendment Request Screen
  3. Review the current application information.
  4. Provide a reason for the amendment. Creating an Amendment Request – Reasons for Amendment
  5. Confirm that the request details are correct.
  6. Click Continue. The system verifies whether the selected record is eligible for amendment processing.

Result: A new amendment request is created and saved in Draft status.

docs.title: Locating an Existing Record
docs.text:
Before creating an amendment request, locate the credit application or account that requires modification.

To locate an existing record:

  1. Navigate to Applications > All Applications Processing Application Screen

  2. Use the search field to locate the application by:

    • Application Reference Number
    • Applicant Name
    • Account Number
    • Other available search criteria Locating an Existing Record – Search Filters
  3. Review the search results.
  4. Select the appropriate record to open the Application Details screen. Submitting an Application – Application Details
  5. Verify that the record is eligible for amendment before proceeding.

Result: The selected application or account record is displayed and ready for amendment processing.

docs.title: Monitoring Amendment Status
docs.text:
After submission, monitor the amendment request throughout the review and approval process.

To monitor amendment status:

  1. Navigate to Applications > My Applications or My Requests.
  2. Locate the amendment request.

  3. Review the current workflow status.

    Amendment Request Workflow Status

    Status Description Draft Amendment request is being prepared and has not been submitted. Submitted Request has been submitted for processing. Under Review Request is being evaluated by a reviewer. Pending Approval Request is awaiting approver decision. Approved Amendment has been approved and applied. Returned Request requires correction or additional information. Rejected Amendment request has been rejected and no changes were applied.

  4. Open the request to view detailed status information, comments, and history. If a request is returned, review the comments provided, make the required updates, and resubmit the request.

Result: Users can track amendment progress and respond to review or approval feedback as needed.

docs.title: Submitting an Amendment Request
docs.text:
Submit the amendment request after all updates and supporting documents have been provided.

To submit an amendment request:

  1. Review all modified information.
  2. Verify that all required supporting documents have been uploaded.

  3. Click Submit Amendment Request. Submitting an Amendment Request

  4. Confirm the submission when prompted. The system performs validation checks to ensure:

    • Required fields are completed.
    • Supporting documents are provided.
    • Uploaded files meet format and size requirements.
    • The requested changes comply with configured business rules.

    If validation fails, the request is returned for correction. Submitting an Amendment Request – Failed Submission Scenario

Result: The amendment request is submitted and progresses to the review workflow.

docs.title: Updating Information
docs.text:
Update the information that requires modification as part of the amendment request.

To update information:

  1. Open the amendment request.
  2. Navigate to the section requiring modification.

  3. Update the necessary fields. Examples of information that may be updated include:

    • Applicant details
    • Contact information
    • Employment information
    • Financial information
    • Credit card details
    • Other application-specific information

  4. Review the modified information for accuracy. Updating Information

  5. Save your changes.

Result: The updated information is stored in the amendment request and remains editable until submission.

docs.title: Uploading Amendment Documents
docs.text:
Supporting documents may be required to justify the requested changes. To upload amendment documents:

  1. Open the amendment request.
  2. Navigate to the Supporting Documents section.
  3. Click Upload Document.
  4. Select the appropriate document category.
  5. Browse and select the file to upload.
  6. Click Upload.
  7. Repeat the process for additional supporting documents if required. The system validates uploaded documents based on configured file type and file size requirements.

Result: The uploaded documents are attached to the amendment request and become available for review. Uploading Amendment Documents

docs.title: Approver Functions
docs.text: This section describes the activities performed by approvers when reviewing requests that have completed validation and review activities and are awaiting a final decision. Approvers evaluate request information, supporting documents, workflow history, and reviewer recommendations before approving, rejecting, or returning requests. Approver Dashboard

docs.title: Approving Requests
docs.text:
Approvers can approve requests that satisfy all review and approval requirements.

To approve a request:

  1. Open the request.
  2. Review all submitted information and supporting documents.
  3. Verify reviewer recommendations and workflow history.
  4. Click Approve Request.
  5. Enter approval comments if required.
  6. Confirm the approval action.

When a request is approved:

  • The request status changes to Approved.
  • The approval decision is recorded in the workflow history.
  • Audit records are generated.
  • Notifications are sent to relevant users.
  • Approved changes or actions are applied to the request.

Result: The request is approved and processing is completed successfully. Approving Request

docs.title: Rejecting Requests
docs.text:
Approvers can reject requests that do not satisfy approval requirements.

To reject a request:

  1. Open the request.
  2. Review the submitted information and supporting documents.
  3. Click Reject Request.
  4. Enter the reason for rejection.
  5. Provide supporting comments.
  6. Click Submit Rejection Decision.

When a request is rejected:

  • The request status changes to Rejected.
  • No further workflow processing occurs.
  • Rejection comments are recorded in workflow history.
  • Notifications are sent to relevant users.
  • Audit records are generated.

Result: The request is rejected and the workflow is terminated. Rejecting Request

docs.title: Returning Requests
docs.text:
Approvers can return requests when additional information, clarification, or corrections are required before a final decision can be made.

To return a request:

  1. Open the request.
  2. Review the submitted information and supporting documents.
  3. Click Return Request.
  4. Enter the reason for the return.
  5. Specify the required corrections or additional information.
  6. Click Submit Return Decision.

When a request is returned:

  • The request status changes to Returned.
  • Return comments become available to the requester.
  • The requester can update and resubmit the request.
  • Workflow history is updated.
  • Audit records are generated.

Result: The request is returned for correction and may be resubmitted after updates are completed. Returning Requests

docs.title: Reviewing Request Information
docs.text:
Approvers can review submitted information before making an approval decision.

To review request information:

  1. Open a request from the Pending Approvals queue.
  2. Review the request summary information.
  3. Verify submitted applicant or account information.
  4. Review workflow history and reviewer recommendations.
  5. Review supporting documents and comments.
  6. Confirm that all approval requirements have been satisfied.

Approvers should verify that:

  • Required information is complete.
  • Supporting documents have been reviewed.
  • Validation requirements have been satisfied.
  • Reviewer recommendations have been provided.
  • Business and compliance requirements have been met.

Result: The approver determines whether the request is eligible for approval. Reviewing Request Information

docs.title: Viewing Pending Approvals
docs.text:
Approvers can access requests that have been routed to them for approval. To view pending approvals:

  1. Navigate to Approvals.
  2. Select Pending Approvals. The Pending Approvals page displays key request information including customer name, product type, priority, status, assigned approver, submission date, and SLA due date.
  3. Review the list of requests awaiting approval.
  4. Use available filters to locate a specific request.
  5. Click the request reference number to open the request details page.

Result: The selected request is displayed for approval review. Viewing Pending Approvals

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This section provides users with a brief overview of the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform, the purpose of the guide, the intended audience, and the primary user roles involved in the credit origination workflow.

docs.title: Purpose of the Guide
docs.text: The User Guide provides instructions for using the CardFlow Credit Origination Platform to create, review, approve, and track credit-related requests. It helps users understand the platform’s features, navigate the user interface, and perform workflow-related activities efficiently.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text: The CardFlow Credit Origination Platform is a multi-tenant SaaS solution designed to automate and manage the end-to-end credit origination lifecycle. The platform supports credit application, amendment, and reinstatement workflows through configurable business rules, validation services, approval routing, notifications, and audit tracking. Users can submit requests, review supporting information, participate in approval workflows, monitor request status, and access workflow history through a centralized web-based interface.

docs.title: Intended Audience
docs.text: The guide is intended for users who interact with the platform as part of the credit origination process, including applicants, tenant users, reviewers, and approvers. The document serves as a reference for performing day-to-day operational activities, understanding workflow progression, and managing requests throughout their lifecycle.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text:
The platform supports multiple user roles, each with specific responsibilities and permissions in the credit origination process.

  • Applicant
    • Creates and submits credit-related requests
    • Provides supporting information and documents
    • Responds to returned requests and monitor application status throughout the workflow lifecycle.
  • Tenant User
    • Manages credit requests on behalf of their organization
    • Creates, updates, submits, and tracks applications, amendments, and reinstatement requests while coordinating with reviewers and approvers
  • Reviewer
    • Assesses submitted requests
    • Validates supporting information and documentation
    • Provides review comments, and either return requests for correction or forward them for approval
  • Approver
    • Evaluates reviewed requests and make final workflow decisions
    • Depending on assigned permissions, approvers approve, reject, or return requests for additional information

docs.title: Credit Reinstatement Requests
docs.text: The Credit Reinstatement workflow enables authorized users to request the reactivation of previously suspended or inactive credit accounts. Reinstatement requests are reviewed and validated before approval to ensure that account reactivation complies with business, operational, and regulatory requirements.

docs.title: Creating a Reinstatement Request
docs.text:
Create a reinstatement request to initiate the account reactivation process.

To create a reinstatement request:

  1. Open the inactive account record.
  2. Click Create Reinstatement Request.
  3. Review the account information.
  4. Provide the reason for reinstatement.
  5. Verify that the request details are correct.
  6. Click Continue. The system validates whether the selected account is eligible for reinstatement processing.

Result: A new reinstatement request is created and saved in Draft status.

Create Reinstatement Request Screen

docs.title: Finding an Inactive Account
docs.text:
Locate the inactive or suspended account that requires reinstatement before creating a reinstatement request.

To find an inactive account:

  1. Open the Applications page.
  2. Use the search field to locate the account by:
    • Application Reference Number
    • Applicant Name
    • Customer ID
  3. Apply filters as needed.
  4. Select Inactive, Suspended, or Closed status.
  5. Open the account record.

Result: The account details page is displayed, showing the current account status and reinstatement eligibility information.

Finding an Inactive Account

docs.title: Providing Supporting Information
docs.text:
Provide supporting details and documentation required to justify the account reactivation request.

To provide supporting information:

  1. Open the reinstatement request.
  2. Navigate to the appropriate section.
  3. Enter the required reinstatement details.
  4. Provide supporting justification.
  5. Upload any required supporting documents.
  6. Save your changes.

Examples of supporting information may include:

  • Updated customer contact information
  • Employment verification
  • Updated financial information
  • Proof of payment or settlement
  • Compliance documentation
  • Account reactivation justification

Result: The supporting information is saved and remains editable until the request is submitted.

Providing Supporting Information

docs.title: Submitting the Reinstatement Request
docs.text:
Submit the reinstatement request after all required information and supporting documents have been provided.

To submit a reinstatement request:

  1. Review the reinstatement request details.
  2. Verify that all required documents have been uploaded.
  3. Click Submit Reinstatement Request.

  4. Confirm the submission when prompted. The system performs validation checks to ensure:

    • Required fields are completed
    • Supporting documentation is provided
    • Uploaded files meet file type and size requirements
    • Reinstatement eligibility requirements are satisfied
    • Business rules and compliance requirements are met

    If validation fails, the request is returned for correction.

Result: The reinstatement request is submitted and enters the review workflow.

Submitting the Reinstatement Request

docs.title: Tracking Reinstatement Progress
docs.text:
Monitor the progress of a reinstatement request throughout the review and approval process.

To track reinstatement progress:

  1. Open the reinstatement request.
  2. Review the status displayed on the request. Tracking Reinstatement Progress
  3. Monitor the workflow timeline.
  4. Review comments and activities provided by reviewers and approvers.

  5. Check notifications for status updates. Typical reinstatement statuses include:

    • Draft
    • Submitted
    • Under Validation
    • Under Review
    • Pending Approval
    • Approved
    • Rejected
    • Returned

Result: Users can monitor request progress, review workflow activities, and determine whether additional action is required. Tracking Reinstatement Progress – Returned Reinstatement
